item.research_question: How does the electronic structure of platinum group metal-based high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles influence their hydrogen evolution reaction activity and stability compared to conventional catalysts?
item.material_system: IrPdPtRhRu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles (approx. 20 at% each of Ru, Rh, Pd, Ir, Pt)
item.processing_route: One-pot polyol process: five metal precursors in equimolar ratio dissolved in H2O, added to preheated triethylene glycol containing PVP (K30, MW ≈ 40,000) at 230 °C, cooled to RT, washed with ethanol/water/ether, and vacuum dried at RT
item.test_conditions: HER activity measured in 0.05 M H2SO4 and 1.0 M KOH electrolytes; scan rate 5 mV s−1; rotation speed 1600 rpm; stability tested via 3000 cyclic voltammetry cycles at 100 mV s−1
key_findings: HEA NPs have a mean diameter of 5.5 ± 1.2 nm and an fcc structure with a lattice parameter of a = 3.856(1) Å.
The valence band spectrum of HEA NPs is broad and featureless without obvious peaks, unlike monometallic NPs which show obvious peaks.
At an overpotential of 25 mV, the turnover frequency (TOF) of HEA NPs was 9.5 times higher than commercial Pt/C in 0.05 M H2SO4.
At an overpotential of 25 mV, the TOF of HEA NPs was 7.8 times higher than commercial Pt/C in 1.0 M KOH.
HEA NPs required overpotentials of 33.0 mV (acidic) and 17.0 mV (alkaline) to achieve 10 mA cmgeo−2, significantly lower than monometallic counterparts.
HEA NPs showed no apparent loss in current density after 3000 cycles, whereas commercial Pt/C lost 35.5 mV in overpotential at 10 mA cmgeo−2.
The high HER activity of HEA NPs does not follow the conventional d-band center theory trend observed for monometallic catalysts.
item.mechanism: The broad and featureless valence band spectrum implies random atomic configurations leading to a variety of local electronic structures and diverse local density of states, which allows for superior HER activity that cannot be simply estimated from the d-band center theory.
item.limitations: The interpretation of properties is challenging; the d-band center theory cannot describe the activity of HEAs due to surface heterogeneity; the authors note deviations in d-band center calculations may originate from differences between NPs and simple slab models.
item.future_work: It would be useful to use a combination of density functional theory calculations and machine learning to understand the reaction mechanism; HEA NPs can be a major future research target given the uncountable combinations.
quotes: The observed valence band (VB) spectrum are broad without any peaks which implies that the HEA NPs have random atomic configurations leading to a variety of local electronic structures.
At an overpotential of 25 mV, the turnover frequencies of HEA NPs were 9.5 and 7.8 times higher than those of a commercial Pt catalyst in 0.05 M H2SO4 and 1.0 M KOH electrolytes, respectively.
The TOF values of IrPdPtRhRu HEA NPs in both acidic and alkaline solutions are very high and do not follow d-band centre theory as expected.
